sources.note: A training-free two-stage prompting protocol that extracts a problem's answer-space constraints first and then checks its own intermediate and final results against them, routed on by a regex detector.
sources.title: Constraint-First Reasoning: A Training-Free Protocol for Exploiting Answer-Space Constraints in Mathematical Problem Solving

sources.note: Formalises implicit agent state that survives session boundaries as Persistent Semantic Entities defined by name binding, event triggering and propagation, and measures across 24 models that whether injected contamination decays depends on what kind of contamination it is rather than on model scale or deployment.
sources.title: Persistent Semantic Entities in Tool-Augmented LLM Systems

sources.note: Replaces reliance on unpredictable emergent 'aha moments' by explicitly aligning models to deduction, induction and abduction on self-verifiable tasks before domain RL.
sources.title: Beyond 'Aha!': Toward Systematic Meta-Abilities Alignment in Large Reasoning Models

sources.note: Trains a sparse autoencoder over whole reasoning steps rather than tokens, conditioning both encoder and decoder on the preceding trajectory so the sparse code carries only what the step adds, and shows that step correctness, logicality, length and first token are all linearly decodable from that code.
sources.title: Step-Level Sparse Autoencoder for Reasoning Process Interpretation

instructions:
Write the wiki definition for 'self-verification'.

The sources below are every archived paper and talk that mentions it. Define it as they use it: if they disagree, say so; if the term is used loosely, say that too.

`related` is the one part of the note nothing can work out on its own. The wiki already links entities that turn up in the same summary; what it cannot see is the neighbour a reader would actually want next — the generation before this one, the benchmark it was built to beat, the method it replaces. Name those. Leave the list empty rather than repeating what the sources already put side by side.

Rules:

- Ground every statement in the supplied material. If something is not stated,
  leave the field empty rather than inferring it.

result.definition: A model checking its own output before committing, and across 4 sources a capability the archive separates from self-correction by what it produces -- a judgement rather than a revision. Its instances: a protocol that extracts a problem's answer-space constraints first and then checks intermediate and final results against them, which grounds the check in something outside the model's own confidence; a meta-abilities framework treating it as one of several alignable capacities; and a step-level decomposition that locates verification behaviour in a trace. The archive's related evidence bounds it sharply: the precision of emergent self-corrections is measured at 24.4 percent, agreement does not track correctness on hard problems, and a persistent-state study finds in-context self-reflection ranging from -14 to +45 percent across models with no reduction at all on one. The pattern is that verification against an external constraint works and verification against the model's own belief does not.
